summary: On the Billboard Pop Shop Podcast, Katie & Keith chat about the late country icon's relationship with pop music over the years.
body: While there’s no question Dolly Parton was popular, she had no intention of “going pop” throughout her 60-plus-year career. On the new Billboard Pop Shop Podcast, Katie & Keith are chatting about the relationship Parton — who died on Aug. 25 at age 80 — had with pop music, from her crossover hits to collaborating with her goddaughter Miley Cyrus. In a 1977 interview with Country Music magazine — the same year she released one of her poppiest hits, “Here You Come Again” — Parton addressed the genre question head-on. “I never considered the fact that I was going pop,” she said at the time. “I will go pop, as far as crossing over, sooner or later. title: PSA: Gemini can adjust system settings on any Pixel running Android 17
summary: Hey Google, make my phone be quiet.
body: TL;DR Pixel 11 debuted a Gemini feature called Device Help that can automatically adjust device settings based on text prompts. Device Help is available on all Pixel phones running Android 17, a Googler has clarified. The feature is also coming to more devices in the future. The Pixel 11 series debuted a new Gemini feature called Device Help . Device Help lets you tell Gemini what you want to accomplish on your phone, and the AI will return the relevant settings and even offer to make multiple changes for you in a single tap. Now, we’ve learned that the feature isn’t a Pixel 11 exclusive. Google’s Minhaz A V recently posted a video of Device Help in action on X . The clip shows Gemini surfacing a set of features to help make the phone “comfortable to use at night,” including dark mode and screen brightness settings. More interestingly, though, the tweet says that Device Help is available on any Pixel phone running Android 17, and that it’s coming to more devices in the future.

title: Pixel 11 owners say their phones are waking up without being touched
summary: The reports on Reddit suggest one gesture is way too sensitive on the latest Pixels.
body: TL;DR Pixel 11 owners report the Lift to check phone feature is waking their screens with very little movement. Some commenters say the feature seems noticeably more sensitive than it was on their older Pixels. Disabling Lift to check phone appears to be the only workaround to stop the issue right now. Now that the Pixel 11 series has only been out in the wild for a short time, the inevitable early quirks are starting to emerge. One of them appears to involve Google’s usually handy ‘Lift to check phone’ feature, with Pixel 11 Pro owners reporting that their screens are waking with barely any movement at all. A Reddit user raised the issue after noticing their new Pixel 11 Pro repeatedly waking while simply sitting on a table. After experimenting with the phone’s wake settings, they found that disabling the gesture stopped the behavior.

title: مورينيو يودع ميسي: مسيرتك لن تُنسى.. وغيابك سيؤثر على المونديال
summary: سبيشيال وان يمدح البرغوث
body: سبيشيال وان يمدح البرغوث علق البرتغالي جوزيه مورينيو، مدرب ريال مدريد، على إعلان ليونيل ميسي، نجم إنتر ميامي وأسطورة برشلونة، بعد إعلان اعتزاله اللعب الدولي. وكتب ميسي، في بيان رسمي، نشره على حسابه بشبكة "إنستجرام ": "بعد مرور كل هذا الوقت منذ المباراة النهائية، وبعد تفكير طويل، أريد أن أعلن للجميع أنني قررت اعتزال اللعب مع المنتخب". يمكنكم مناقشة الموضوعات والأخبار بشكل أعمق في منتديات "كووورة" وأضاف: "كان قرارًا مؤلمًا وما زال يؤلمني في أعماقي، لكنني أدرك أن الوقت قد حان. أقسم لكم أنني دائمًا قدمت كل ما لدي، ليس فقط خلال السنوات الأخيرة التي حققنا فيها كل شيء، بل قبل ذلك أيضًا، ودائمًا ما قاتلت وبذلت كل ما أملك من أجل هذا القميص، ومن أجل إسعادكم وجعلكم تشعرون بالفخر بكونكم أرجنتينيين من خلال كرة القدم". وكتب مورينيو تعليقا على منشور ميسي، قائلا: "تهانينا لك على مسيرة دولية رائعة ولا تُنسى. لن تكون بطولة كوبا أمريكا المقبلة وكأس العالم المقبلة بغيابك كما كانتا من قبل". title: رادار الاتحاد يلتقط جناح أستون فيلا
summary: الاتحاد يُكثف تحركاته بحثا عن تدعيمات جديدة في الخط الأمامي
body: الاتحاد يُكثف تحركاته بحثا عن تدعيمات جديدة في الخط الأمامي يُكثّف نادي الاتحاد تحركاته في سوق الانتقالات الصيفية الجارية، بحثًا عن تدعيمات جديدة في الخط الأمامي، مع اقتراب إغلاق باب القيد. وكشفت صحيفة " الشرق الأوسط " أن إدارة الاتحاد تدرس دعم مركز الجناح بأحد نجوم أستون فيلا الإنجليزي، في ظل الحاجة إلى إضافة لاعب يملك السرعة والخبرة في الملاعب الأوروبية. وأكدت أن العميد وضع عينيه على الجامايكي ليون بايلي "29 عامًا" جناح أستون فيلا، الذي سبق له خوض تجربة بارزة مع باير ليفركوزن الألماني، قبل أن ينتقل إلى الفيلانز، كما خاض فترة قصيرة بقميص روما الإيطالي. تذاكر مباريات دوري روشن السعودي اشترِ تذكرتك الآنَ! وشارك الجناح الجامايكي مع أستون فيلا في 163 مباراة في مختلف البطولات، أحرز خلالها 23 هدفًا، وأسهم بـ25 تمريرة حاسمة. ولا يقتصر بحث الاتحاد على بايلي؛ إذ كان اسم الكولومبي ياسر أسبريلا، جناح جيرونا الإسباني، قد برز سابقًا ضمن قائمة المرشحين لتقوية الخيارات الهجومية للفريق قبل إسدال الستار على فترة الانتقالات الصيفية، وفقا للمصدر نفسه. اقرأ أيضا: 15 مليون يورو لا تكفي؟.. بنفيكا يغلق بابه في وجه الاتحاد اقرأ أيضا: رجل المستحيل.. رئيس الأرجنتين يودع ميسي

title: Google finds another way to push Search users to AI Mode
summary: AI Overviews are automatically expanding for some searches.
body: TL;DR Some Google Search queries are returning fully expanded AI Overview summaries. These expanded summaries include a text box labeled Ask anything that links to AI Mode. It seems this is only the case on desktop. Google’s been working at making AI Mode a more prominent part of Search for some time. Now, it’s taken another step to that end: some AI Overview summaries are now showing up fully expanded, complete with a text box where you can type follow-up questions that’ll launch an AI Mode interaction. Previously, these text boxes only appeared when you clicked Show more at the bottom of an AI Overview. This change hasn’t been officially announced, but was recently pointed by co-founder of SEO agency Nectiv Chris Long on X (via WinFuture ). Today, certain search terms return results that begin with an expanded AI Overview answer that takes up quite a bit of space, along with a box labeled Ask anything, inviting users to stay inside Google’s ecosystem rather than scrolling down to the websites it’s pulling information from.

title: Satellite SOS just proved why it could be your phone’s most important feature
summary: Satellite connectivity reportedly helped one survivor reach rescuers during the deadly Nepal flooding disaster.
body: Credit: Mishaal Rahman / Android Authority TL;DR A survivor of the tragic Nepal flood disaster says satellite connectivity helped him contact rescuers after conventional networks went down. He was reportedly able to reach a helicopter and was evacuated from the disaster area. The case shows the potentially life-saving value of satellite features being adopted by major phone manufacturers. Satellite connectivity has gradually become a more familiar smartphone feature in recent years, offering a way to call for help when conventional networks aren’t available. The technology has now reportedly proved its worth during the tragic Tibet-Nepal flooding, with one survivor saying it helped him contact rescuers and escape to safety. As reported by PhoneArena , a survivor caught up in the disaster said he was able to maintain communication with the outside world via satellite connectivity on his HUAWEI Mate X5 after regular network service was lost. He later posted about his experience on the social media account of HUAWEI Executive Director Richard Yu.

title: Galaxy Z Fold 8 is selling so well, Samsung is borrowing parts from the future
summary: The company is reportedly using future component reserves to fill the gap.
body: TL;DR Galaxy Z Fold 8 demand is reportedly outpacing Samsung’s expectations. A Display Driver IC (DDI) shortage is now putting pressure on Fold 8 production. Samsung is tapping future DDI reserves to keep making current Fold 8 units. Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra just became the best-selling Android phone globally in Q2 2026, while the regular Galaxy S26 also cracked the top 10. Now, Samsung has another phone that people apparently want more than it expected — so much so that the company is reportedly dipping into component stock reserved for future production to keep the Galaxy Z Fold 8 coming. According to ZDNet Korea , Samsung is running short of the Display Driver IC (DDI) used to control the pixels on the Galaxy Z Fold 8 OLED display. Samsung has reportedly increased its component orders after demand for the passport-style foldable exceeded expectations. But its DDI supplier, Taiwan’s United Microelectronics Corporation (UMC), has little room to ramp up production.

title: New Android 17 QPR2 feature lets you peek inside your phone’s secure sandbox
summary: Android 17 QPR2 Beta 4 introduces new Private Compute Core data logging controls inside Privacy Dashboard.
body: Credit: Joe Maring / Android Authority TL;DR Android 17 QPR2 Beta 4 adds a dedicated “Data logging” menu for Private Compute Core within Privacy Dashboard. Users can toggle logging between Limited (up to three days/100MB) and Detailed (up to 12 hours/100MB) tiers, download logs, or delete them. Google rolled out Android 17 QPR2 Beta 4 , and alongside several under-the-hood tweaks, it introduces a major transparency upgrade for how the OS handles sensitive on-device data. The new release adds a dedicated “Data logging” section for the Private Compute Core right inside Privacy Dashboard. Private Compute Core is Android’s isolated sandbox that powers machine learning features such as Live Caption, Now Playing, and Smart Reply, without exposing user data directly to the cloud or other apps. While Private Compute Core has historically operated in a secure silo, this new Privacy Dashboard entry in Android 17 QPR2 Beta 4 lets users actively monitor, log, and review any outbound data leaving the Private Compute Core environment.

But the market doesn’t always make things so simple for us, and this year with Google’s new Pixel 11 series, some shoppers might want to take a long, hard look at exactly what those upgrades offer — and what Google wants us to pay for them. title: ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude quietly get worse over time. This hidden setting fixes them
summary: Your favorite AI chatbot might be remembering a little too much.
body: I’ve been using LLM-based AI in some capacity for roughly half a decade, and in that time, the industry has changed significantly. Not only have newer competitors like Gemini and Claude arrived on the scene, but older tools like ChatGPT have also evolved dramatically. We’ve seen better third-party app integration, increased reasoning capabilities, and countless other advancements. However, I would argue that the ability to retain memories matters most. Retaining context from previous conversations helps the AI better anticipate your needs within a single session. It also allows the tool to learn more about you, ensuring that future conversations are tailored to your preferences. However, there is a real downside to memory accumulation that not everyone considers. I’ve found that starting with a new AI usually requires significant input to generate the responses I need and fully understand my user profile. Once it reaches this data “sweet spot,” the AI becomes much more pleasant to use. Yet, slowly over time, the experience often seems to degrade again.

Let’s start with the good USB-C news for the Pixel 11 Pro XL. After years of underperforming the headline charging figure, Google’s latest large flagship comes much closer to hitting its 45W marketing claim. title: Meta fixes distressingly obvious smart glasses recording LED loophole

It turns out this check was only performed when recordings were initiated, and users could just start filming and cover the LED afterwards. Meta is currently rolling out a fix to correct this behavior. Retro gamers may remember the old PlayStation 1 swap trick: The system would only check disc integrity when first booting, so you could run imports or backups by first powering the PlayStation up with a legit disc in it, and then quickly swapping it out. It turns out that Meta’s smart glasses have been vulnerable to a similar attack, and the company is only just now getting around to patching it. Everybody’s concerned about smart glasses and privacy right now, and probably the biggest issue there is centered on surreptitious recording.
